en: A space launch vehicle is a rocket that carries satellites or space probes into space beyond Earth. Korea successfully launched Naro in 2013, but Naro's first-stage rocket was built in cooperation with Russia. So the Korea Aerospace Research Institute set a goal of completing the entire process—from design to production, testing, and launch operation—with domestic technology, and began developing Nuri, Korea's own space launch vehicle.

Nuri is a three-stage launch vehicle about 47 meters long. Its first stage bundles four 75-ton-class liquid engines together to produce powerful thrust, and the second and third stages separate one after another to carry the satellite up to its target altitude. There were many mountains to climb, such as the technology to bundle several engines and run them together and the technology to build huge fuel tanks, and many Korean companies took part in making parts and solved these problems together.

In its first launch in October 2021, Nuri failed to place a satellite model into the target orbit. However, the researchers found the cause and fixed it, and in the second launch in June 2022, Nuri safely placed a performance verification satellite into orbit. In the third launch in May 2023, it put several working satellites into orbit. With this, Korea became the seventh country in the world to launch a satellite weighing more than one ton with its own technology.

In May 2024, the Korea AeroSpace Administration (KASA), a government agency in charge of space and aviation policy, opened its doors. KASA takes the role of leading both research and development and the growth of the industry. Space development is a comprehensive industry where technologies from many fields—machinery, electronics, and software—come together, so it is connected to a wide range of career paths. Because independence in launch vehicle technology is the starting point for moving on to satellite use and space exploration, Nuri's success is regarded as an event that opened a new chapter in Korea's space development.

en: The DNA inside a living thing's cells contains the genetic information needed for life. A gene is a unit of information that determines an organism's appearance and physical traits. "Genetic scissors" is a general term for technologies that find and cut a specific part of this DNA. Among them, CRISPR is a third-generation genetic scissors that appeared around 2012; because it is easier to make and costs less than earlier technologies, it changed the course of life science research around the world. The name CRISPR comes from a repeating DNA sequence structure discovered in bacteria.

The principle of CRISPR came from the immune system of bacteria. When a bacterium is infected by a virus, it records a piece of the virus's genes in its own DNA, and when the same virus invades again, it recognizes that part and cuts it. Scientists applied this principle and paired two elements: a guide RNA that leads the way to the target DNA, and the Cas9 protein that actually cuts that spot. Thanks to this, it became possible to select and cut a gene at the desired location.

Emmanuelle Charpentier and Jennifer Doudna, who laid the foundation for this technology, received the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 2020. CRISPR is widely used in research to uncover the causes of genetic diseases and to find treatments, and in 2023 a CRISPR-based treatment was approved for the first time in the world. This treatment is used to treat blood diseases caused by genetic abnormalities. In agriculture, CRISPR is used to develop crops that resist disease or are rich in nutrients.

Of course, there are also limits and controversies. Errors can occur in which the wrong part is cut instead of the target, and once a gene has been changed, it is hard to undo. In particular, editing the genes of reproductive cells, which are passed directly on to offspring, raises such serious ethical debate that many countries strictly regulate it. For CRISPR to benefit humanity, careful social agreement is needed as much as technological progress.

en: Artificial intelligence that answers questions as if having a conversation and writes texts on request is now widely used. AI that creates new results such as text, images, and sounds is called generative AI. Behind it lies a technology called the large language model. A model means something built to imitate a real-world process so that a computer can handle it. A language model is a program that calculates, using probability, in what order words are likely to follow one another.

A language model learns by reading vast amounts of text, such as books and internet documents. It repeats, countless times, the exercise of covering part of a sentence and guessing the word that comes next. This process of learning in advance is called pre-training. During this process, the countless parameters inside the model are adjusted little by little, and grammar, knowledge, and ways of expression soak into it. Once training is complete, when the model receives a question, it produces an answer by joining high-probability words one by one.

Generative AI helps with many kinds of work, from writing and translation to summarizing long texts and even writing computer programs. Many people also use it to refine their ideas or to study foreign languages. Because of this, the way people work is changing in many fields, including education, journalism, and industry. Still, one thing does not change: it remains a tool that supports human judgment.

However, its limits are also clear. A language model only produces plausible-sounding sentences based on probability; it cannot check for itself whether the content is true. This leads to the hallucination phenomenon, in which it states wrong information with confidence. There is also a risk that it learns and copies the biases contained in the texts it studied. In addition, it may not know about news that appeared after its training ended. This is why the habit of critically reviewing AI answers and checking their sources is so important.

en: Population structure is a framework that shows how a population is composed by age, gender, and other factors. It changes according to the number of people who are born, who die, and who move in or out. Korea is experiencing two phenomena at the same time: low birth rates, in which fewer babies are being born, and population aging, in which the share of elderly people in the total population is rising. According to surveys by the Ministry of Data and Statistics, these trends have continued steadily over many years.

In general, a society is called an aging society when people aged 65 or older make up more than 7% of the population, an aged society when they exceed 14%, and a super-aged society when they exceed 20%. Korea has recently entered the stage of a super-aged society, and the speed of this change is very fast even by world standards. As average life expectancy grows longer and the number of newborns falls, the shape of the population pyramid is also changing into a form that is narrow at the bottom and wide at the top.

Changes in population structure affect many areas of society. When the number of students falls, schools and the education system are adjusted, and when the working-age population that can hold jobs shrinks, companies find it harder to secure workers. On the other hand, demand for medical and care services grows, and the silver industry, which serves elderly people as its main customers, expands. How to run systems that generations pay for together, such as pensions and health insurance, is also being discussed again. In some regions, the population is shrinking and the vitality of local communities is weakening.

In response, the government is acting with a variety of policies. Typical examples are support systems that create a good environment for having and raising children, and programs that help elderly people with jobs and health. Because population change appears gradually over a long period, it is important to prepare in advance on the basis of accurate statistics. Understanding population structure is a starting point for looking ahead to the future of our society.

en: The overall level of the prices of goods and services traded in the market is called the price level. The price level is not the cost of one individual product; it combines the prices of many products to show an average trend. The Consumer Price Index that appears in the news is an indicator that expresses the movement of prices as a number. The phenomenon of prices rising continuously is called inflation, and when it occurs, the value of money falls relatively. This is because the amount of goods that can be bought with the same money decreases.

The basic principle behind price movement is supply and demand. When the demand to buy a product is greater than its supply, the price rises, and when supply is greater than demand, the price falls. Prices can also rise when the costs of making a product, such as raw material prices or wages, go up. When these factors appear across many products, the overall price level moves.

If prices rise or fall too quickly, the whole economy becomes unstable. That is why the Bank of Korea, the country's central bank, takes price stability as its most important goal. The Bank of Korea raises or lowers the base interest rate to influence the amount of money circulating in the market. When interest rates rise, consumption and investment decrease, which can have the effect of calming price increases. Conversely, when the economy slows down too much, the bank may lower interest rates to stimulate economic activity.

Meanwhile, the wages that working people receive have a lower limit set by law. The minimum wage system is designed to guarantee a minimum level of wages and protect low-paid workers. The minimum wage is deliberated and decided every year by the Minimum Wage Commission, in which members representing workers, members representing employers, and members representing the public interest take part. The commission considers a range of factors, such as workers' cost of living, the wages of similar workers, and labor productivity, and once the government confirms and officially announces the decision, it applies the following year.

en: Every year, a large amount of plastic waste flows into the sea. Much of it comes from land. Trash thrown away on the streets travels with rainwater and rivers until it reaches the sea, and nets and buoys thrown away or lost during fishing also remain in the ocean. Trash floating on the sea sometimes travels far offshore along ocean currents. Plastic is convenient because it is light and strong, but it is a material that takes a very long time to break down in nature.

Plastic that enters the sea is gradually broken into small pieces by the action of waves, ultraviolet rays from sunlight, and salt. Pieces that have become smaller than 5 millimeters across are called microplastics. Microplastics may be particles made small from the start, or fragments created when larger plastics break apart. Because they are so small, they spread widely through the water and are very hard to remove. Such tiny pieces are found not only in seawater but also in mudflats and on sandy beaches.

Plastic waste causes many kinds of harm to the marine ecosystem. When seabirds and turtles mistake plastic for food and swallow it, their digestive organs can become blocked, and animals caught in abandoned nets sometimes lose their lives because they cannot move. Microplastics have been confirmed to move along the food chain, from plankton to fish, so scientists are continuing to study their effects. The coastal scenery is also damaged, hurting tourism and fishing.

Responses are being made on several levels. The government and the Korea Marine Environment Management Corporation collect trash from beaches and the sea and run programs to reduce fishing waste. The international community is discussing an agreement to reduce plastic pollution. Individual efforts, such as using fewer disposable products and sorting waste for recycling, are also important. The surest way to reduce the plastic heading to the sea is to produce less waste in the first place.

en: Gases in the atmosphere such as carbon dioxide and methane trap heat rising from the Earth's surface and keep the planet's temperature stable. This is called the greenhouse effect, and such gases are called greenhouse gases. The greenhouse effect itself is a natural phenomenon that is essential for life. However, fossil fuels such as coal, oil, and natural gas release carbon dioxide when they are burned. Since industrialization, the use of fossil fuels has increased greatly, raising the concentration of greenhouse gases in the atmosphere, and the Earth's average temperature has risen along with it.

To respond to climate change, the international community signed the Paris Agreement and promised to keep the rise in the Earth's average temperature below a certain level. The goal set for this purpose is carbon neutrality. Carbon neutrality means reducing greenhouse gas emissions as much as possible and offsetting the remaining emissions through absorption by forests or storage technology, so that net emissions become zero. Many countries, including Korea, have declared carbon neutrality as their goal.

The key means is energy transition. Renewable energy comes from sources that nature supplies continuously and that never run out, such as sunlight, wind, and water. Solar power uses the principle that solar cells made of semiconductors produce an electric current when light falls on them. In wind power, the wind turns large blades, and a generator converts that rotation into electricity. Because no fuel is burned, almost no greenhouse gases are released while the electricity is being generated.

Still, the challenges are clear. Renewable energy is intermittent, meaning its output changes with the weather, so devices that store electricity and improvements to the power grid are needed. The large amount of land and money needed for power facilities, and consultation with local residents, are also important issues. That is why technologies that use energy efficiently and habits of saving energy are emphasized together. Improving the insulation of old buildings also helps save energy. Carbon neutrality is a goal that can be reached only when technology, institutions, and citizens' actions work together.

en: The Veritable Records of the Joseon Dynasty is a vast collection of history books that organizes the records of the reigns of Joseon kings. At its foundation was the court historian system. Historians attended meetings between the king and his officials and wrote down the king's words and actions, along with affairs of the state large and small, in records called sacho. Because the principle that even the king could not freely read the sacho was upheld, historians could record the facts without worrying about those in power.

The Veritable Records were not compiled while a king was still alive. Only after a king died was a temporary office called the Sillokcheong set up and compilation begun. Its officials gathered and reviewed the sacho and documents from each government office, arranged them in order of time, and completed the records. When the compilation was finished, the sacho were washed in water to erase the writing, a practice called secho. This was done to prevent the contents of the records from leaking out and causing conflict.

Several copies of the completed records were made and stored separately in archives called sago. Even if the records in one archive were destroyed by fire or war, the copies elsewhere would survive. In fact, during the Japanese invasions of Korea in the 1590s, most of the archives burned down, but the copy at the Jeonju archive alone survived. After the war, Joseon made several new copies based on the surviving records and moved the archives deep into the mountains, where access was difficult, to keep them even safer.

The Veritable Records of the Joseon Dynasty cover the history of one dynasty over several hundred years almost without gaps. They record not only politics and diplomacy but also weather, astronomical events, and the daily lives of the people, making them precious material for historical research. In recognition of this value, the records were inscribed in UNESCO's Memory of the World register in 1997. Today the records have been translated into modern Korean, and anyone can look them up on the internet. The spirit of record-keeping that protected five hundred years of Joseon history still lives on.

en: In 1443, King Sejong the Great created a new writing system called Hunminjeongeum, and in 1446 he proclaimed it to the people. Hunminjeongeum means "the correct sounds for teaching the people." At the time, there were no Korean letters for writing the Korean language, so people borrowed Chinese characters, but these were hard to learn and difficult for ordinary people to use. King Sejong wanted to create letters that anyone could easily learn and use, in order to ease the hardship of people who could not put into writing what they wished to say.

The consonants of Hunminjeongeum were created on the principle of imitating shapes. The five basic consonants copy the shapes of the speech organs as each sound is made. The letter ㄱ imitates the shape of the root of the tongue blocking the throat, and ㄴ the shape of the tongue touching the upper gums. The letter ㅁ came from the shape of the mouth, ㅅ from the shape of a tooth, and ㅇ from the shape of the throat. The remaining consonants were made by the principle of adding strokes to the basic letters. Since strokes are added as the sound becomes stronger, you can guess the nature of a sound just by looking at the shape of the letter.

The vowels begin from three basic letters that stand for heaven, earth, and human. The round dot ㆍ symbolizes heaven, the horizontal line ㅡ the flat earth, and the vertical line ㅣ a standing person. By combining these basic letters with one another, many vowels such as ㅏ and ㅗ were created in a systematic way. This method of writing countless sounds by combining a small number of basic letters according to fixed rules is highly efficient.

When Hunminjeongeum was created, it had twenty-eight letters in all: seventeen consonants and eleven vowels. Today, 24 of them are in use. The purpose and principles behind the letters are explained in detail in a book called the Hunminjeongeum Haerye, the explanatory edition. It is rare anywhere in the world for records to remain showing who created a writing system, when, and on what principles. In recognition of this value, the Hunminjeongeum Haerye was inscribed in UNESCO's Memory of the World register in 1997.

en: Webtoons are digital comics that developed to fit the internet environment. They began to grow in earnest in the early 2000s, when Korean internet portals started serializing comics for free. At a time when the print comics market was struggling, webtoons opened a way to meet readers in a new space, the internet. Because anyone could access them easily, the readership expanded quickly, and the culture of communicating with readers through comments also added to the popularity of webtoons.

The most distinctive feature of the webtoon format is vertical scrolling. Unlike paper comics, which are read by turning pages, webtoons are read by scrolling down the screen. This style suits smartphone screens well, so people can read comfortably even while on the move. New storytelling techniques that make use of this vertical flow have also developed, such as adjusting the blank space between panels to express the passage of time or a feeling of tension.

Webtoons gradually formed an industrial ecosystem of their own. A partial-payment model, in which readers pay a fee to read some episodes in advance, took hold and created a stable revenue structure. Beyond authors and platforms, many other participants appeared, such as agencies that support authors and production studios where the writing and the drawing are handled by different people. Before a single webtoon is created and reaches its readers, many different jobs work together.

A webtoon's story does not stay inside the webtoon alone. Popular works are remade into dramas, films, games, and more. This spreading of an original story into many fields is called the expansion of intellectual property, or IP. Korean webtoon platforms have also expanded their services into many languages and gained readers overseas. The vertical-scroll format that took root in Korea has now become one of the standard formats for digital comics in many countries around the world.

en: Space is filled with high-energy particles that fly in from the Sun and from the distant universe. These are called space radiation. On Earth, the thick atmosphere and the magnetic field act as shields, so people live without serious harm. The Moon, however, has almost no atmosphere and only a very weak magnetic field, so space radiation pours straight down onto its surface.

Space radiation can damage the cells of the human body, so astronauts must prepare for it before staying on the Moon for a long time. That requires accurate data showing how strong the radiation on the lunar surface actually is and what kinds of particles arrive in what amounts. Only with accurate data can we decide how to build spacesuits and lunar bases. Data from the Moon's south pole, which many countries are watching as a candidate site for future crewed exploration, is especially important.

The lunar surface space radiation detector LVRAD, which is being developed under the leadership of the Korea Astronomy and Space Science Institute, is the instrument in charge of this task. It consists of a device that measures the amount and energy distribution of radiation and a device that measures neutrons. In August 2026, the Korea AeroSpace Administration signed an implementing arrangement with the U.S. National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) to send the detector on a lunar lander built by an American private company.

According to the plan, the detector will finish development by 2027 and then be moved to the United States, and it will head for the Moon's south pole aboard a lander launching in 2030. However, the launch date may change depending on NASA's schedule. The observation data gathered there will be used to study how space radiation affects the human body and to prepare for future crewed lunar exploration. It is also a chance for Korea to take on a role in international lunar exploration and show the world the level of its space science.

우주방사선은 태양에서만 날아오므로, 태양에서 멀리 떨어진 천체라면 방사선을 걱정할 필요가 없을 것이다.

challenge.explain: 0문단에서 지구는 두꺼운 대기와 자기장이 방패 역할을 해 주고, 달은 대기가 거의 없고 자기장이 약해 방사선이 그대로 내리쬔다고 했습니다. 이 원리를 적용하면 보호막이 약한 천체의 표면에는 지구보다 강한 방사선이 도달할 것입니다. '방패'라는 본문 표현을 그대로 쓴 첫 번째 선지가 헷갈리지만, 본문은 '두꺼운' 대기가 막아 준다고 했으므로 얇은 대기만으로 충분하다고 볼 근거가 없고, 방사선은 태양뿐 아니라 먼 우주에서도 날아온다고 했으므로 두 번째 선지도 어긋납니다.

en: The main cause of climate change is the greenhouse gases released when fossil fuels such as coal and oil are burned. The problem is that if companies can release greenhouse gases for free, they have no reason to spend money on reducing their emissions. So many countries have devised a way to put a price on pollution. Policies that make emitters pay for their carbon emissions are broadly called "carbon pricing." A leading example of such a policy is the greenhouse gas emissions trading scheme.

The emissions trading scheme rests on two pillars: a cap on total emissions and trading. First, the government sets the total amount of greenhouse gases that can be emitted across the whole country. Within that limit, it distributes emission allowances to companies. One unit of allowance is the right to emit one ton of greenhouse gases. In principle, a company can emit only as much greenhouse gas as the allowances it holds.

The key point is that allowances can be bought and sold in a market. A company that invests in technology to reduce greenhouse gases and has allowances left over can sell them and make a profit. In contrast, a company that runs short of allowances must buy them from the market. The higher the price of allowances rises, the more advantageous it becomes to cut one's own emissions rather than to buy. The system was designed so that reducing pollution literally pays.

Korea has been operating an emissions trading scheme since 2015, and allowances are traded on the Korea Exchange like stocks. The scheme covers more than 70% of the country's total greenhouse gas emissions, and about 770 companies are taking part in the fourth planning period, which began in 2026. Allowance prices move with the economy and with policy, and recently they have also swung sharply. Following the signals the price sends, companies draw up their plans for reducing emissions.

en: Just as there are heatwaves on land, there are heatwaves in the sea. A 'marine heatwave' is a period in which the sea water stays much warmer than the normal level for that region and season for five days or more. Scientists usually use a standard: the water temperature must be high enough to rank in the top 10% of the records from the past thirty years. Because sea water holds heat longer than air, a marine heatwave, once it starts, can sometimes continue for weeks.

According to an analysis released by the Korea Meteorological Administration in August 2026, marine heatwaves occurred in the seas around Korea for an average of 83.3 days per year during the last ten years (2016-2025). That is 3.7 times the normal level. During the same period, the sea surface temperature was also 0.7 degrees higher than normal. The KMA expects that if warming continues, marine heatwaves will become more frequent and stronger, and by the end of the century most days of the year could be marine heatwave days.

When the sea gets hotter, the effects spread both inside and outside the ocean. Fish species that live in cold water move north, changing the kinds of fish that are caught, and fish on farms die in large numbers because they cannot stand the high water temperature. A hot sea also supplies the air with a great deal of heat and water vapor, which fuels heatwaves and heavy rain and makes typhoons stronger. The changes in the sea come back to us as the weather on land.

So scientists watch the water temperature in real time with satellites and observation equipment at sea, and when it rises sharply, they issue warnings so that fishing communities can prepare. Cutting greenhouse gas emissions can also slow down the warming of the ocean. For marine scientists and climate researchers who study marine heatwaves, and for people in the fishing industry who look for ways to adapt to a changed sea, the warming ocean is becoming a stage for new careers.

en: Colorectal cancer can be treated well when it is found early. But colonoscopy, the main screening test, requires a hard preparation process to empty the bowel, and the simple stool test has limits in accuracy. So many people put off getting screened. Recently, a new possibility was suggested to lower this barrier: a test that screens for the risk of colorectal cancer with just one blood draw.

When cells in our body die or break apart, they release small pieces of DNA into the blood. These floating pieces are called 'cell-free DNA.' The pieces released by cancer cells are slightly different from those of normal cells in their length, their end structures, and where they sit in the genome. In other words, they are traces that cancer cells leave in the blood. A test that reads the state of the body from fluids like blood is called a 'liquid biopsy.'

The problem is that these differences are too small for human eyes to pick out. This is where artificial intelligence shows its power. In August 2026, a research team at Asan Medical Center announced the results of a study that used AI to analyze blood data from 1,677 people, including colorectal cancer patients and healthy people. The sensitivity for finding cancer patients was 90.4%, and the specificity for correctly identifying healthy people was 94.7%. The test also kept high performance for early-stage cancer.

What would change if testing became easier? If a simple blood draw could screen for risk, people who have been putting off screening would get tested earlier, and there would be more chances to find cancer at an early stage. However, this is only a screening test that filters out the possibility of cancer. To confirm a diagnosis, a colonoscopy and a biopsy are still needed, and the test must pass more verification before it is used in real screening programs.

Research like this is completed through the cooperation of many experts: doctors who treat patients and collect data, life scientists who study the features of cell-free DNA, and medical AI developers who build models that learn patterns. Whether you are interested in medicine, life science, or artificial intelligence, this field keeps a door open where they all meet.

en: In the heart of Seoul stand two UNESCO World Heritage sites. One is Changdeokgung, a palace of the Joseon dynasty, listed in 1997. The other is Jongmyo, the shrine that holds the spirit tablets of Joseon's kings and queens, listed in 1995. Wooden pillars and tiled roofs catch the eye first, but beneath them thousands of stones form the platforms, stairs, and walls that hold the buildings up.

Since 2023, the National Research Institute of Cultural Heritage of the Korea Heritage Service has been carrying out a project to study these stones scientifically. Researchers examined all 4,421 stones one by one — 2,922 at Changdeokgung and 1,499 at Jongmyo — and identified what kind of rock each one is. They then marked the results in color on drawings of the buildings, creating 'rock maps' that were shared with the public.

The survey showed that most of the stones are pale pink granite. More than 90% of the stones at Changdeokgung and over 99% at Jongmyo are this rock. The same pale pink granite is found on mountains around Seoul, such as Inwangsan, Ansan, Bukaksan, and Bukhansan. This suggests that the builders may have brought the stones from mountains not far away.

Why does it matter where the stones came from? Stone looks strong, but over many years it weathers, cracks, and breaks off. If a damaged stone is replaced with one from a different source, the color and texture will not match, and it may weather at a different speed, spoiling the look of the heritage site. That is why the survey also compared granite from the Seoul and Pocheon areas. The data will serve as basic material for choosing stones for future repair and restoration.

This survey brought together petrology, the study of rocks, and conservation science, which protects cultural heritage. Conservation scientists use knowledge from chemistry, geology, and biology to analyze what heritage objects are made of and how damaged they are, and to find ways to treat them. It is a fitting career for someone who loves old things and scientific inquiry at the same time.

en: Electricity is invisible, but it is a product that costs more the farther it travels. As it flows through power lines, some of it is lost as heat, and building and managing the transmission network also costs a great deal of money. In Korea, however, nuclear power plants and renewable energy facilities are concentrated in the southern regions, while the factories and data centers that use a lot of electricity are concentrated in the capital area. The places that make electricity and the places that use it are far apart.

On August 26, 2026, the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment and the Korea Electric Power Corporation held a public hearing and unveiled a draft design for a regional electricity pricing system for industry. By adding a new 'regional adjustment rate' to the current bill, the plan divides the country into eleven regions and applies different industrial rates to each. In the southern regions, which are close to power plants, rates would fall by up to 18 won per kilowatt-hour, about 10% of the average industrial price. Jeju, as an island with special conditions, was left out of this plan.

In economics, a price is a signal. If rates differ by region, companies that use a lot of electricity will consider cheaper regions when they build factories or data centers. The government hopes this signal will spread industrial facilities away from the capital area, cutting transmission costs and boosting local economies.

Of course, there are open questions. When companies choose a location, they weigh many conditions besides electricity rates, such as workers, transportation, and distance to business partners, so some point out that a rate gap alone may not actually move factories. Others worry that regions may clash over gains and losses. The plan is not a finished system yet; it is a draft that will be revised based on opinions gathered at the hearing.

This news connects to many careers. Engineers who design transmission networks and power systems, business experts who calculate rates and locations to shape company strategy, and policy experts who turn rate systems into laws and rules all work on top of this design. Reading the signal called price is a tool they all share.

en: On August 27, 2026, Korea's Ministry of Education announced that classroom teachers will lead the development of textbooks and learning materials for the new artificial intelligence (AI) subjects taught in schools. Through an open call, sixteen subjects were selected: six for elementary school, two for middle school, and eight for high school. This is the first time the government has supported textbook development for AI subjects.

Korean textbooks are divided into three types according to how they are developed. Government-designated textbooks are written directly by the state. Authorized textbooks are made by publishers and must pass a national screening. Approved textbooks are reviewed and approved by provincial offices of education so that schools can use them; their procedures are relatively flexible, which suits newly created subjects well. The new AI textbooks will be developed as approved textbooks.

Until now, many schools offered AI-related classes without official textbooks, so teachers had to create their own materials every semester, which was a heavy burden. In this project, classroom teachers join as authors and lead the whole process, from analyzing the curriculum and organizing units to writing the manuscript. Their real experience of teaching students goes straight into the textbook.

The plan also reflects how fast AI technology changes. The main textbook will contain core concepts and principles that last a long time, while the latest technology trends and hands-on examples will be made as separate booklets or web-based materials that are updated continuously. The finished textbooks will be tried out in schools in the first semester of 2027 and, after review and approval by provincial offices of education, used in classes from March 2028.

The main characters of this change are today's students, because they will be the first generation to learn AI with these new textbooks. If teaching attracts you, you can dream of becoming a teacher; if you want to support learning with technology, an edtech developer; if you like explaining knowledge in a simple way, an educational content creator. Knowing how textbooks are made is the first step.

challenge.q: 새 교과서를 2028년 정식 사용 전에 2027년 1학기에 학교 현장에 먼저 시범 적용하는 까닭으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: 시도교육청의 인정 심의를 이미 통과했음을 보여 주기 위해서
실제 수업에서 써 보며 부족한 점을 확인하고 다듬기 위해서
최신 기술 동향을 별책 자료에 담기 위해서
교원이 교육과정 분석부터 집필까지 주도했음을 알리기 위해서
challenge.explain: 시범 적용은 정식 사용 전에 실제 교실에서 미리 써 보는 단계이므로, 부족한 점을 확인해 더 나은 교과서로 다듬으려는 목적이라고 추론할 수 있다. 인정 심의를 통과했음을 보여 준다는 첫 번째 선지가 그럴듯하지만, 넷째 문단에서 시범 적용을 거친 뒤에 시도교육청의 인정 심의를 받는다고 했으므로 순서가 어긋난다. 별책 자료는 최신 내용을 갱신하기 위한 장치일 뿐 시범 적용의 목적이 아니다.

금속 작품은 보존 처리가 필요 없다.
밝은 곳에 두면 모든 작품이 오래간다.
challenge.explain: 같은 미술관 안에서도 재질에 따라 허용 조도가 80럭스에서 1500럭스까지 벌어진다. 기준을 가르는 것은 값이나 유명세가 아니라 빛에 견디는 성질이다.

choices: 즉시 색이 바랜 부분을 덧칠해 복원한다.
먼저 상태조사로 손상 부위를 기록한 뒤, 온습도와 조도를 맞춘 수장고에 보관한다.
밝은 전시실에 걸어 관람객이 많이 보게 한다.
습기를 없애려고 난방기 옆에 둔다.
challenge.explain: 기록을 근거로 삼는 절차와, 처리보다 앞서는 사전 관리라는 두 원칙을 함께 지킨 것은 2번뿐이다. 덧칠은 근거 없는 처리이고, 밝은 빛과 난방기는 글이 경계한 조건이다.

en: A work of art begins to change the moment it is finished. Pigments lose their brightness, paper oxidizes and turns yellow, and cracks appear on the surface. The activity of slowing this damage and extending the life of a work is called conservation science. Because it demands both a knowledge of art history and the chemistry needed to analyze materials, conservation science sits on the border between art and science.

Korea's National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art is the country's only national institution devoted to art conservation. It divides the work into four fields, paper, oil painting, sculpture and craft, and material analysis, and looks after some 8,000 works. A conservator does not touch a piece right away. A condition survey comes first, recording where and how badly the work is damaged, and that record becomes the basis for deciding how to treat it. Leaving a reason behind matters more than the treatment itself.

In practice, the larger share of conservation is not repair but prevention. The museum keeps galleries and storage rooms at 18 to 22 degrees and holds relative humidity between 50 and 70 percent. Too much moisture invites mold, and too little makes surfaces crack. Lighting also differs by material. Oil paintings are limited to 150 lux or less, ink and watercolor paintings to 100 lux, and dyed works and prints to 80 lux. Metal and stone, which resist light well, may be shown at up to 1,500 lux.

Contemporary art makes conservation harder still. Nam June Paik's The More, the Better is a tower of 1,003 cathode ray tube monitors rising 18.5 meters. When it was shut down in 2018 because of age, the museum spent three years restoring it. Seven hundred and thirty-seven damaged monitors were repaired with secondhand parts, and 266 that could no longer be used kept their outer shells while flat panels replaced the inside. Preserve the original form, or preserve the ability to run? A conservator has to choose, again and again.

books.note: 국립현대미술관 보존과학자가 쓴 책. 실제 작품이 어떻게 진단되고 처리되는지를 사례로 보여 준다. 이 글의 배경을 그대로 넓혀 준다.

books.author: 파비에네 마이어·지빌레 불프
books.note: 복원 전문가 두 사람이 그림 한 점이 되살아나는 과정을 그림과 함께 풀어낸 청소년 책. 초·중등이 먼저 읽기 좋다.

papers.title: 국립현대미술관 보존과학 연구
papers.note: 미술관이 공개한 보존처리·재질분석 연구 자료로, 실제 작품이 어떤 절차를 거쳤는지 확인할 수 있다.

questions.q: 이 글의 중심 내용으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: 카페인은 아데노신 수용체를 차단하여 졸음을 느끼지 못하게 한다.
아데노신은 몸에 해로운 물질이므로 없애야 한다.
커피는 청소년의 성장에 도움이 된다.
잠을 잘 자려면 규칙적으로 운동해야 한다.
questions.explain: 글은 카페인이 아데노신 대신 수용체에 결합해 졸음 신호를 차단하는 원리를 중심으로 설명하고 있다.

questions.q: 아데노신이 수용체와 결합하면 우리 몸에 나타나는 변화는 무엇인가?
choices: 심장이 빨리 뛴다.
정신이 맑아진다.
신경 활동이 느려지고 졸음을 느낀다.
분자 구조가 바뀐다.
questions.explain: 첫째 문단에서 아데노신이 수용체와 결합하면 신경 활동이 느려지면서 피로와 졸음을 느끼게 된다고 하였다.

questions.q: '아데노신의 작용을 차단해'에서 '차단'의 문맥상 의미로 가장 알맞은 것은?
choices: 여러 가지를 차례대로 늘어놓음
가로막아서 작용하지 못하게 함
두 물질을 섞어 하나로 만듦
높은 곳에서 낮은 곳으로 옮김
questions.explain: 카페인이 수용체 자리를 먼저 차지해 아데노신이 결합하지 못하도록 막는다는 뜻이므로, 차단은 가로막아 작용하지 못하게 하는 것을 의미한다.

questions.q: 카페인의 효과가 사라진 뒤 다시 졸음이 밀려오는 까닭으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: 아데노신이 모두 분해되었기 때문에
수용체의 수가 줄어들기 때문에
카페인이 아데노신으로 변하기 때문에
쌓여 있던 아데노신이 다시 수용체와 결합하기 때문에
questions.explain: 카페인은 수용체 자리만 차지해 아데노신을 막고 있을 뿐이므로, 카페인이 사라지면 그동안 쌓인 아데노신이 다시 수용체와 결합해 졸음을 일으킨다고 추론할 수 있다.
